div.head: Had 3
div.ab: And to hádbote, gif feorhlira wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam oðrum stæpe twa pund to bóte mid godcundran scrifte.
⁊ to hádbóte, gif feorhlyre wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam oðrum stæpe twa pund to bóte mid godcundan scrifte.
⁊ to hadbote, gif feorhlyre wurþe, toeacan þam rihtwere, æt þam oðran stæpe II pund to bote mid godcundan scrifte.
Et ad emendationem ordinis, si uitę sit amissio, supra rectam weram in secundo gradu due libre emendentur (reddantur) cum Deo digna penitentia.
And to hadbote, gif feorhlyra wurðe, toeacan þam rihtwere æt þam oðran stæpe II pund to bote mid godcundan scrifte.
Und wenn Verlust des Lebens [eines Klerikers] eintritt, [zahle Verletzer] ausser dessen gesetzlichem Wergeld, bei dem zweiten Ordo als Klerusbusse 2 Pfund zur Busse, neben geistlicher Poenitenz.
And if loss of life [of a cleric] occurs, [let the offender pay], besides his lawful wergild, for the second grade 2 pounds as compensation for orders, with spiritual penance.

And as compensation for one in orders if loss of life occurs, the perpetrator must make amends for the second rank by paying two pounds in addition to the standard wergild and by doing spiritual penance.

[And in compensation for [an offence against a man in] orders, if loss of life occurs, one must pay for the second degree with two pounds in addition to the legal wergild, and intercede zealously with ecclesiastical penance.
div.note: U: not in Whitelock’s English Historical Documents, which prints only Had 1–2 and 9–11 (with “…” for the rest); the source of this translation is not recorded.
